newsitem.title: PORTUGAL: Portugal cereal production seen down this year.
newsitem.headline: Portugal cereal production seen down this year.

text.p: Production of cereals is expected to ease in Portugal this year, compared with 1996, following a drought, the National Statistics Institute said.
"Autumn/winter cereals did not recover from a period of drought in the first months of the year, and so there is a generalised drop in production," a statement said.
"Production of wheat, rye, oats and barley should fall by 30 percent, 23 percent, 30 percent and 39 percent, compared with 1996 levels," it added.
In the previous harvest, the production of wheat was 1.714 tonnes per hectare, rye was 0.884 tonnes per hectare, oats 0.857 tonnes per hectare and barley 1.527 tonnes per hectare.
According to the latest available estimates from INE Portugal, Europe's smallest cereals producer, harvested around 415,000 tonnes of wheat in 1996, up from 360,000 tonnes the previous year.
Portugal harvested 63,000 tonnes of oats, 58,000 tonnes of barley and 44,000 tonnes of rye.
